items.title: Skyscraper in Riyadh damaged as Saudi Arabia reports surge in new Houthi attacks
items.summary: A skyscraper in Saudi Arabia's capital Riyadh was damaged on Thursday after the Gulf country reported new attacks by Yemen's Houthis. Witnesses said the city's Public Investment Fund Tower, which showcases Saudi Arabia's economic ambitions, was "damaged across several floors, with windows blown out".
items.t: Skyscraper in Riyadh damaged as Saudi Arabia reports surge in new Houthi attacks

items.title: Gaza: Israel launched new offensive on Nuseirat
items.summary: Israeli tanks have moved east of the Nuseirat refugee camp in central Gaza, with witnesses reporting heavy shelling, gunfire and airstrikes as the Israeli military says it has launched an operation in a Hamas-controlled area. Strikes killed at least three people on Wednesday, and displaced families are fleeing again, saying there is no real ceasefire. Israel and Hamas accuse each other of breaking the truce in force since October 2025, while Gadi Eisenkot tries to form a government after inconclusive elections.
items.t: Gaza: Israel launched new offensive on Nuseirat

items.title: APEC summit: Trump seeks nuclear arms cuts, but few concrete results expected
items.summary: Donald Trump has arrived at the APEC summit for talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin, but expectations for concrete results are low. Nothing substantial is likely to come out of the meeting, as was the case in his previous encounters with the two leaders, says Fraser Jackson, FRANCE 24’s correspondent in Washington. The main issue on the table is nuclear disarmament, with Trump seeking to get the United States and China to reduce their stockpiles. The wars in Iran and Ukraine are also expected to feature in the discussions.
items.t: APEC summit: Trump seeks nuclear arms cuts, but few concrete results expected

items.title: Beijing summit: AI and tech competition between US and China
items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping is welcoming US President Donald Trump and Russia’s Vladimir Putin on Thursday for the first-ever three-way summit between the leaders. Beyond the wars in Ukraine and Iran, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies are expected to feature in the talks between Washington and Beijing, as the two powers compete for the lead in AI, advanced chips and other strategic technologies. FRANCE 24's
items.t: Beijing summit: AI and tech competition between US and China

items.title: Iran ramps up attacks on Gulf countries after U.S. strikes
items.summary: America's Persian Gulf allies and oil tankers are under fire as Iran appears to lash out following U.S. strikes on a key island in the Strait of Hormuz.
items.t: Iran ramps up retaliation on Gulf countries after U.S. strikes

items.title: Trump, Xi, Putin set for rare joint meeting in China
items.summary: President Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin are about to hold a rare face-to-face meeting in China.
items.t: Trump and Xi speak at APEC summit ahead of rare joint meeting with Putin

items.title: Tammy Shipley was supposed to be monitored in prison. Instead she died after drinking 20L of water
items.summary:
If the Aboriginal woman had been checked at regular intervals as required, her ‘excess consumption of water’ would have been prevented, inquest finds

• Warning: This article contains images of and references to Indigenous Australians who have died

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The death of an Aboriginal woman who collapsed after drinking at least 20 litres of water in a New South Wales prison cell was preventable and the result of systemic failures, a coroner has found.

Tammy Michelle Shipley, 47, died at Silverwater women’s correctional centre on 20 December 2022.

Continue reading...
items.t: Tammy Shipley was supposed to be monitored in prison. Instead she died after drinking 20L of water

items.title: Mother whose twin baby died was determined to have home birth despite advice of experts, NSW inquest hears
items.summary:
Inquest into deaths of four babies in northern NSW between 2022 and 2024 told mother refused to give birth in hospital after hearing others’ traumatic stories

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Baby B’s mother was so determined to have a home birth she ignored the advice of experts – including her own midwife, an inquest has heard.

The inquest heard she was pregnant with twins, which she described as a “wonderful shock”, and didn’t want a hospital birth because she had heard of others’ traumatic experiences.

Continue reading...
items.t: Mother whose twin baby died was determined to have home birth despite advice of experts, NSW inquest hears

items.title: FIFA rankings: France finish the year on the podium, Morocco break into the top five
items.summary: FIFA unveiled its final world ranking of 2026. France remain third in the world, behind Spain and Argentina. Les Bleus have now finished in the top three for the ninth consecutive year. Morocco climb two places to fifth, equalling the best-ever ranking by an African nation, previously achieved by Nigeria in 1994. Brazil drop to seventh, while Senegal remain 18th and Ivory Coast sit 28th.
items.t: FIFA rankings: France finish the year on the podium, Morocco break into the top five

items.title: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?
items.summary: The sharp sell-off in tech stocks after the US midterms and the Nvidia scandal has cast doubt on Anthropic's IPO. Yet with hundreds of billions still being invested, some think the AI party is still in full swing.
items.t: Is the AI bubble bursting just as Anthropic goes public?

items.title: ‘Remarkable luck’: wreck of first Australian-built warship discovered exactly 128 years after sinking
items.summary:
HMCS Spitfire was commissioned by colonial government to protect against Russian warships during the Crimean war

The wreck of Australia’s first locally built warship has been discovered 128 years after sinking off the coast of far north Queensland.

Marine archaeologists found the remains of Ex HMCS Spitfire on 21 August, the anniversary of its sinking in 1898.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘Remarkable luck’: wreck of first Australian-built warship discovered exactly 128 years after sinking

items.title: Middle East crisis poses 'largest threat' to energy security in history, warns IEA
items.summary: The International Energy Agency said on Thursday that the Middle East crisis triggered by US and Israeli strikes on Iran in February posed the “largest threat” to energy security in history. It warned that consumers were bearing more of the costs as Iran’s blockade of the Strait of Hormuz disrupted oil shipments.
items.t: Middle East crisis poses 'largest threat' to energy security in history, warns IEA

items.title: Datacentres to create 70% more carbon emissions by 2030, IEA report warns
items.summary:
Global energy watchdog forecasts huge rise as US and China turn to fossil fuels to power AI growth agendas

The world’s datacentres will create 70% more carbon emissions within the next four years as the US and China turn to fossil fuels to power their AI growth agendas, according to the world’s energy watchdog.

The International Energy Agency (IEA) warned that datacentres will consume twice as much electricity by 2030 compared with today, with the global expansion of artificial intelligence accounting for three-quarters of this growth.

Continue reading...
items.t: Datacentres to create 70% more carbon emissions by 2030, IEA report warns

items.title: General Pants Co enters voluntary administration, putting hundreds of jobs at risk
items.summary:
Australian fashion chain becomes latest retailer in trouble after David Jones, Cue and Veronika Maine

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The youth fashion chain General Pants Co has become the latest major retailer to slide into voluntary administration, putting nearly 500 jobs at risk as Australia’s retail sector continues to struggle with cash-strapped shoppers and online-only competitors.

The collapse comes not long after that of the upmarket department store David Jones and premium womenswear brands Cue and Veronika Maine, underscoring the mounting toll of tough economic conditions on established retailers.

Continue reading...
items.t: General Pants Co enters voluntary administration, putting hundreds of jobs at risk

items.title: ‘Shame old Aussies’ to ‘fresh chaos’: what the UK papers say about Bancroft’s explosive ball tampering claims
items.summary:
Sports sections of British newspapers deliver their take on the unfolding Cricket Australia sandpaper saga

The sports sections of the UK’s major mastheads are relishing the never-ending crisis engulfing Australian cricketing, after a key player in the ball tampering controversy, Cameron Bancroft, alleged everyone on the team knew about the 2018 plot.

Bancroft’s allegation came five days after a lengthy media conference by the current Australia Test captain, Pat Cummins, during which he denied that everyone on the team was in on the sandpaper plan. Cummins was responding to the allegation first aired in teammate Usman Khawaja’s biography, that actually, everyone did know about the sandpaper Bancroft was later caught holding.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘Shame old Aussies’ to ‘fresh chaos’: what the UK papers say about Bancroft’s explosive ball tampering claims

items.title: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN
items.summary:
Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds

One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.

In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.

Continue reading...
items.t: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN

items.summary: Vanuatu's Environment Minister Ralph Regenvanu has called for changes to the UN climate summit process, accusing a small group of countries of blocking progress and warning that COP31 risks reversing previous commitments.

items.summary: The leaders of China, the US and Russia are set to hold a first-of-its-kind trilateral meeting on Thursday in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, on the sidelines of an APEC summit. The meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, which Beijing said would involve "safeguarding world peace", has raised fears of a carve-up of the globe into "spheres of influence". Follow our liveblog for the latest developments.

items.title: Almost 1 in 4 children live in conflict zones — report
items.summary: Denial of humanitarian access, abductions and sexual violence are among several violations against children that have increased dramtically over the past year, according to a new report by Save the Children.
items.t: Almost 1 in 4 children live in conflict zones — report

items.title: Mike Lynch’s superyacht had unidentified vulnerability to high winds, report finds
items.summary:
Bayesian, which sank off Sicily killing seven including tech tycoon, had not been fully assessed, say investigators

The superyacht Bayesian, which sank in a storm off Sicily killing seven people including the tech tycoon Mike Lynch and his teenage daughter, was vulnerable to knockdown but crew were not aware as it had never been assessed at anchor with its sails down, the final report from the UK’s Marine Accident Investigations Branch (MAIB) has said.

The 56-metre (184ft) vessel was anchored near the fishing port of Porticello when it sank during a violent storm shortly before dawn on 19 August 2024.

Continue reading...
items.t: Mike Lynch’s superyacht had unidentified vulnerability to high winds, report finds

items.title: Crimea bridge has been attacked again, says Russian-installed governor
items.summary:
Assessment of damage is underway, days after two attacks that destroyed road section of key bridge across Kerch strait linking annexed peninsula to Russia

A key bridge connecting annexed Crimea to Russia has been attacked again, a Russian-appointed regional governor has said, two days after Ukrainian strikes caused serious damage to it.

“Following a new attack on the Crimean Bridge, traffic has been temporarily halted. All relevant services are on site and at work. An assessment of the damage is under way,” Sergei Aksyonov, the Kremlin-appointed governor of Crimea, wrote on Telegram. The Russian transport ministry said on Thursday that no one was wounded in the attack and that train services across it had been halted.

Continue reading...
items.t: Crimea bridge has been attacked again, says Russian-installed governor

items.title: EU proposes €45bn loan for Ukraine to avert cash crisis and boost defences
items.summary:
Von der Leyen says she wants to give Kyiv ‘strong hand’ in talks and is confident all 27 member states will back idea

The EU executive has proposed a €45bn (£37.5bn) loan for Ukraine to help with a looming cash crisis and reinforce its defences, as Russia’s relentless bombardment continues.

Announcing the plan to lend Kyiv the money in 2027, the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, said: “We think this is the best way to give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiating table. And Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused in Ukraine.”

Continue reading...
items.t: EU proposes €45bn loan for Ukraine to avert cash crisis and boost defences

items.title: 24-month matured Comté crowned world’s best cheese
items.summary: With its nutty flavour and smooth, supple texture, it was aged for two years in a former military fortress in eastern France. Comté, an unpasteurised cow’s milk cheese from the Jura Mountains, has beaten more than five thousand challengers to the top prize at the prestigious annual 'World Cheese Awards'. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington has the story.
items.t: 24-month matured Comté crowned world’s best cheese

items.title: Florida pastor found guilty over 2021 assassination of Haitian president
items.summary:
Christian Emmanuel Sanon faces life in prison after conviction on charges arising from killing of Jovenel Moïse

A Florida pastor with dual Haitian-American citizenship was convicted on Wednesday of US charges arising from the 2021 assassination of the Haitian president Jovenel Moïse.

Christian Emmanuel Sanon was found guilty on charges including conspiring to kill Moïse after a nearly eight-week trial in federal court in Miami. He had faced a total of eight charges including conspiracy to kidnap or kill a person outside the United States.

Continue reading...
items.t: Florida pastor found guilty over 2021 assassination of Haitian president

items.title: Inside Limoges City Hall devastated by arson attack
items.summary: Work is underway to restore the city hall of Limoges, in central France, which was devastated by an arson attack during riots on October 17. More than €1.7 million has been raised through an online fundraising campaign in the wake of the disaster. Also on the show, the highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI has finally been released, with gamers in Oceania among the first to get a taste of the latest instalment in the video game franchise.

items.title: Crimea bridge strike: Fact-checking fake videos of damage after Ukraine's attack
items.summary: Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea, but not all the dramatic footage circulating online is real. Multiple AI-generated videos falsely show the bridge collapsed with extensive damage. Some even used branding resembling a Ukrainian news agency to appear credible. While the bridge was indeed struck and damaged, the viral videos were fabricated using AI, as Vedika Bahl explains.
items.t: Crimea bridge strike: Fact-checking fake videos of damage after Ukraine's attack

items.title: Bassirou Diomaye Faye excluded from Senegal's ruling party
items.summary: In tonight's edition, the political divorce between Senegal's president and the powerful former prime minister and mentor is official. Also, all of Nigeria's states have shown willingness for a push to create their own police forces. And  in parts of the continent, conflict and a drop in funding have placed huge pressures on children's learning.
items.t: Bassirou Diomaye Faye excluded from Senegal's ruling party

items.title: Reconstruction begins at Limoges City Hall after devastating fire
items.summary: It's been a month since the nationwide protests that degenerated in violence across France. The dramatic pictures of the historic City Hall in the French city of Limoges set on fire made headlines worldwide. To the relief of many, the reconstruction work on the building has now begun. Since the fire, donations have poured in and already about 80 percent of the necessary funding has been secured. FRANCE 24's Caitlin Brown reports.
items.t: Reconstruction begins at Limoges City Hall after devastating fire

items.title: Hegseth uses Venezuela visit to boast of Maduro’s capture by US military
items.summary:
Defense secretary asserts US dominance on trip that would have seemed ‘impossible, almost unbelievable’ a year ago

Pete Hegseth has used his first visit to Venezuela since US special forces abducted its former president, Nicolás Maduro, to boast of the dictator’s capture during what he called “the single most sophisticated military operation in the history of Latin America”.

Maduro was controversially seized by Delta Force operatives in the early hours of 3 January, setting in motion an improbable rapprochement between Washington and Venezuela’s anti-imperialist “Chavista” regime, which has ruled since 1999.

Continue reading...
items.t: Hegseth boasts about Maduro’s capture while vowing to deepen US military cooperation with Venezuela

items.title: US Democrats nominate Jeffries to be first Black House speaker
items.summary: Hakeem Jeffries is on the cusp of becoming the first Black speaker of the US House of Representatives after Democrats elected him their leader Wednesday following a sweeping midterm election triumph. Jeffries faced no declared challenger, although opposition from some newly elected progressives had exposed divisions over how Democrats should wield their newfound power. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from Washington.
items.t: US Democrats nominate Jeffries to be first Black House speaker

items.title: Israeli army launches ground operation in Hamas-controlled area of Gaza
items.summary: The Israeli military said it had launched an operation on Wednesday in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza, where an AFP journalist saw Israeli tanks position themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp. The rare ground operation comes after inconclusive Israeli elections, with the opposition's Gadi Eisenkot trying to form a government without caretaker prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who has built his brand on saying he will ensure Israel's security. FRANCE 24's Daniel Whittington reports.
items.t: Israeli army launches ground operation in Hamas-controlled area of Gaza

items.title: 'Netanyahu's only 2 tickets are racism or starting a war: He stopped acting as a democratic player'
items.summary: François Picard is pleased to welcome Israeli writer and filmmaker Etgar Keret, author of "The Seven Good Years", joining us from Tel Aviv. Keret argues that Netanyahu is seeking to remain in power, at any cost, including delegitimizing Arab parties and prolonging conflict. “For him, it could be a never-ending war as long as he's in power. He has no incentive to stop it,” he warns. Keret also calls for Israelis to examine how the war in Gaza was conducted, arguing that “the media as a whole ignored the war.”

items.title: Xi welcomes Trump: Does Nvidia scandal upend US-China AI race?
items.summary: You can strike Jensen Huang from the guest list but good luck steering dinner conversation away from the topic in Shenzhen. The co-founder of the AI computing leader was to accompany the US president to the APEC summit before he was undone by revelations of a dalliance with a Chinese national that happened to coincide with a Singapore client's backdoor skirting of sanctions on its powerful H200 chips.

items.title: EU ‘to close door’ to talks on long-term UK ties until Burnham has decided on Brexit
items.summary:
Diplomats say piecemeal approach of resets is coming to an end and Europe wants clarity on whether Britain wants to reverse its exit

The EU will shut the door to discussions with Andy Burnham about the UK’s longer-term relationship with the bloc until the government has decided whether it wants to proceed with reversing Brexit, diplomats have said.

European capitals are also warning they have reached the end of the line for piecemeal “reset” summits with the UK and want the prime minister to focus on his next steps domestically before they proceed.

Continue reading...

No 10 is confident the PM can make the case for closer EU ties, while others worry about leaving the campaign solely in his hands

The launch of a pro-Brexit campaign was one of the few genuine surprises this week in Westminster, even if the arguments were straight out of a familiar playbook.

The video launched on X over the weekend, with scenes of riots in France, champagne flowing in Brussels, and European politicians saying how desperate they were for Britain’s cash.

items.title: Why Ukraine keeps trying to bring down Russia's bridge to Crimea
items.summary: A Ukrainian drone and missile strike on Monday night brought down a stretch of the bridge linking the annexed Crimean Peninsula to Russia, potentially crippling a route long used by Moscow to move men and materiel into Crimea and the southern front. Here’s why Kyiv keeps testing its strength against an infrastructure project that has become synonymous with Russian President Vladimir Putin’s 2014 seizure of the peninsula.

items.title: Beijing has supported Moscow but 'China understands that America is way more important than Russia'
items.summary: Following Xi Jinping's very friendly rare tarmac greeting for Donald Trump, Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Kerry Brown, Professor of Chinese Studies and Director of the Lau China Institute at King's College, London. Brown examines the complex relationship between the world's two largest economies, China's growing diplomatic influence and the competition over artificial intelligence.“China is the diplomatic center of the world,” says Brown, pointing to Beijing's ability to bring together leaders from Russia, the United States, Europe and elsewhere. He argues that China now has “extraordinary convening power" and significant influence over Russia.

items.title: Apec summit as it happened: Xi welcomes Trump on China visit as Putin claims Europe in ‘humiliating decline’
items.summary:
This blog is now closed, you can read more on this story here

Yalta became a byword for betrayal. Will Trump, Xi and Putin enact another carve-up?

That is the question the Guardian’s diplomatic correspondent Patrick Wintour seeks to address in his piece about the expected, Putin, Trump and Xi, meeting at Apec on Thursday.

It is a truism in diplomacy that if you are not around the table, the risk is that you, or your values, are on the menu and about to be carved up. Many excluded from the summit in Shenzhen, principally Ukraine but also eastern Europe and Baltic countries, Taiwan and even Iran, have reason to be nervous that their sponsors might abandon them in a complex geopolitical trade-off that Putin envisions, and Trump seems to endorse.

Continue reading...
items.t: Apec summit live: Xi and Putin give opening speeches as world leaders gather in China

items.title: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling
items.summary:
A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza

Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay, if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.

The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

items.title: European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt
items.summary:
Leaked documents raise questions about claims Egypt met welfare targets to qualify for €2.5bn in loans

The European Commission has been accused of sugarcoating figures to enable it to release funds to Egypt under a landmark pact with the authoritarian government of Abdel Fatah al-Sisi.

The charge relates to a €7.4bn deal promised by Ursula von der Leyen, the European Commission president, to al-Sisi on a high-profile visit to Cairo in 2024. The three-year “strategic and comprehensive partnership” was intended to bolster Egypt’s shaky economy, deter migrants from coming to Europe and shore up a region reeling from the 7 October attacks and Israel’s war on Gaza.

Continue reading...
items.t: European Commission accused of sugarcoating figures to release funds to Egypt

items.title: South Korea’s high-stakes university exams upended by AI cheating scandal
items.summary:
South Korea has been gripped by revelations of AI-aided cheating, just days before more than half a million students are to sit high-stakes entrance exams

The integrity of South Korea’s career-defining university entrance exam has been thrown into doubt after the top scorer in a recent professional exam admitted using a concealed camera and AI to cheat.

On Thursday, more than half a million people, mostly school students, are due to sit the exam, known as the suneung, at 1,312 centres across the country. The exam runs for a gruelling eight hours over a single day and determines which university a candidate can attend and, in turn, their future prospects.

Continue reading...
items.t: Sleeve checks and no smartglasses: South Korea races to protect all-important university exams against AI

items.title: Caribbean nations fear economic impact of shuttering citizenship program after EU threats
items.summary:
St Kitts and Nevis to wind down citizenship-by-investment program after EU warns of end to visa-free access

The decision by St Kitts and Nevis to end a lucrative programme offering citizenship to wealthy foreigners in exchange for investment threatens its economy and ability to support people in need, the premier of the island of Nevis has warned.

On Friday, Terrance Drew, the prime minister of the twin-island Caribbean nation, announced he would wind down the citizenship-by-investment (CBI) programme, after the European Union threatened to end visa-free access for St Kitts and Nevis.

items.summary:
Indigenous Awá people of Amazon make contact with villagers and accept food to take back to territory

About 20 Indigenous people emerged from isolation in Brazil’s Amazon rainforest, several organizations reported on Tuesday, raising the alarm about increased invasions into the tribe’s territory.

According to the NGO Survival International, members of the Awá people, who live in voluntary isolation, arrived on Monday in a village and made contact with a government team in a “historic encounter”.

items.title: Eight-year-old Haitian boy returns home after release from ICE custody
items.summary:
Child reunited with family after he was detained by immigration agents in San Diego and transferred to Texas

An eight-year-old Haitian boy who was put into restraints and detained by immigration agents in San Diego on 4 November and transferred to a facility in Texas has been reunited with his family in California.

Representative Juan Vargas shared a photograph of the boy and his family in a social media post on Monda, writing: “11 days ago, an 8-year-old in San Diego was taken into federal custody during an immigration check-in. He was separated from his loved ones and held in a facility in Texas. Today, he’s finally home.”

items.title: Five EU states announce plans for immigration ‘return hubs’ in Rwanda
items.summary:
Germany, Austria, Netherlands, Denmark and Greece likely to face challenges to policy criticised as ‘grave moral failing’

Five EU member states have announced plans to set up an offshore centre in Rwanda for people with no legal right to stay in Europe, in a pilot scheme that is expected to face legal challenges and has been denounced as “a grave moral failing”.

The five countries – Germany, Austria, the Netherlands, Denmark and Greece – are the first to seek to use the EU’s newly agreed returns law that allows people who have exhausted all avenues of appeal against their removal from Europe to be sent to a third country.

An American basketball player has been arrested in Nigeria for allegedly attempting to smuggle 33.95kg (75lb) of marijuana into the country.

Nigeria’s National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said a 28-year-old player named as Greene Da’monte Khiree from the state of Georgia was arrested at Lagos’s main airport last Wednesday after he arrived on a flight from Thailand via the United Arab Emirates.
